reward-hacking.what: The loop optimizes the letter of its reward instead of the goal - Goodhart's law in production. It games its own success signal (ships busywork, self-reports success, satisfies a metric that no longer measures value).
reward-hacking.ask: Is the reward a proxy the agent can satisfy without doing the real work? What does the loop gain points for that a human would not call progress?

false-green.what: A quality gate reports success while the work is not actually good: vacuous tests, tautological assertions, skipped cases, or a grader that cannot fail.
false-green.ask: Could this gate be green on broken code? What is the smallest wrong change that still passes it?

stage-timeout.what: A hard per-step wall-clock cap (beneath any outer timeout you set) silently kills work that runs too long. The narration drops and the step looks like it produced nothing.
stage-timeout.ask: What is the hardest time cap actually enforced on one step, and how close is the real work to it?

verdict-token.what: A machine-parsed decision token is missing or malformed, so a downstream parser reads the absence as the pessimistic default and discards good work.
verdict-token.ask: If the step is killed before it writes its decision, what does the parser assume - and is that assumption safe?

steering-channel.what: The channel meant to steer the loop (injected instructions, pinned notes) is not actually delivered - it is truncated, mis-parsed, or dropped by the consumer that was supposed to read it.
steering-channel.ask: Did the CONSUMER's own parser emit the steering text verbatim, or did you only confirm you wrote it?

ipc-and-env.what: The loop breaks on its runtime environment rather than its logic: a rotated socket, an expired credential, an inherited stale variable, the machine going to sleep.
ipc-and-env.ask: What environmental state did this process capture at launch that can change underneath it while it runs?

concurrency.what: Independent agents or sessions contend for one shared resource - a rate-limited API quota, a git index, a working tree - and degrade or corrupt each other, often silently.
concurrency.ask: How many live agents share this one resource right now, and what happens to the one you are waiting on when a second appears?

vcs-destruction.what: Version control is used as a weapon against the working tree: a blanket stage sweeps in unrelated edits, a revert-to-remote discards uncommitted work, or identity leaks into history.
vcs-destruction.ask: Whose uncommitted work is in this tree, and what does a failure-path reset or a blanket 'add all' do to it?

delegation.what: A sub-agent re-delegates instead of doing the work: it spawns another loop, scaffolds a plan for a future iteration, and exits successfully having produced nothing.
delegation.ask: Does the instruction forbid EVERY escape hatch - nested agents, scaffolding a loop, handing off to a later iteration - by name?

detector-fail-open.what: A monitor or safety check silently never fires: a wrong regex flavor, the wrong parsed field, a case mismatch. A negative result is mistaken for health.
detector-fail-open.ask: Have you fed this detector a known-bad sample and watched it fire, AND a known-good sample and watched it stay silent?

detector-fail-closed.what: A monitor or check fires when it should not: it reports a correct artifact as broken, an honest quote as fabricated, a live process as dead. The accusation is specific and plausible, so the natural response is to repair the artifact - which is the destructive direction.
detector-fail-closed.ask: Before acting on this check's accusation, have you verified the ACCUSATION against the primary source - and could the check's own normalisation, base path or parser be the thing that disagrees?

stale-module.what: A long-running process runs the code it imported at launch. Later commits to that module are inert while git and the changelog report them shipped.
stale-module.ask: When did this process start, and how many commits to the code it imported have landed since - with no reload or restart?

checkpoint.what: An all-or-nothing step loses everything when it is interrupted, because it writes its output only at the end instead of writing a minimal-but-complete artifact first and refining in place.
checkpoint.ask: If this step is killed at minute 8 of 10, does a usable artifact already exist on disk?

tooling-paths.what: The shell or tool layer betrays you: command substitution runs inside a string you meant as data, a built-in resolves paths from an unexpected root, an interpreter shim mutates the wrong environment.
tooling-paths.ask: Will any character in this string be interpreted rather than stored, and from what directory does this tool actually resolve paths?

test-isolation.what: A test passes only in the environment where it was written: it depends on untracked local state, ambient file counts, a directory name, or git history a clean checkout does not have.
test-isolation.ask: Would this test pass in a throwaway fresh clone on a different machine? What ambient state is it silently reading?

observability.what: The signal you trust hides the truth: an outcome flag masks a chronically over-budget step, a lifetime average hides a spike, a hardened process reports zero usage.
observability.ask: Are you reading a distribution or a single number, a delta or a lifetime average - and could the measurement itself be denied?

spec-and-scope.what: The loop does the wrong amount of work: it pursues the whole visible mission instead of its assigned slice, or picks tasks by lowest effort instead of highest value, or grows an artifact without bound.
spec-and-scope.ask: Does the agent's visible context imply a bigger goal than its assigned task, and is any required-reading artifact growing every iteration?

identity-and-keying.what: Two distinct things share one identifier or cache key, so state computed for one is served for the other: a slot number a rejection recycles, a cache keyed on a mutable name, a record cited by its position in a re-sorted list.
identity-and-keying.ask: Is this key unique across everything it will ever be asked about, or only across the subset that succeeded?

incidents.title: Reward hacking: twelve near-identical features shipped as different work
incidents.rule: A loop that meets its reward but not its goal is Goodhart's law in production. Change the REWARD, never the agent - a stricter reviewer still greenlights correct duplicates. Add a cross-iteration novelty signal (a scout that reviews the last N ships and vetoes clones), and put the brake in the PLANNER's prompt, not the coder's.
incidents.signature: The loop keeps shipping green work, but if you diff the last N ships they are progressively similar to prior ones. Every iteration passes review; every artifact is individually correct.

incidents.title: The hard per-step wall-clock cap is the number-one cause of lost work
incidents.rule: A per-step timeout you did not set is often the real timeout. If a step's attempt logs are all the same tiny size, its median is AT the cap, not near it. Fix: write-early checkpoint (minimal complete output first, then refine in place), and always report the duration DISTRIBUTION, never a single-shot healthy flag.
incidents.signature: Every attempt log for a specific step is exactly the same tiny size and reads only 'timed out after 600s'. Two full iterations produce nothing while sibling teams on the same infrastructure ship normally.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - the orchestrator whose hard per-stage cap this describes; the cap is enforced by the agent CLI beneath the timeout the loop sets itself.

https://github.com/jeffma8888/proactive-loop-agent - the product loop whose planning stage burned two consecutive iterations this way: 8 attempts, 8 timeouts, ~9 hours, no output, every attempt log 48 bytes.

incidents.title: A slow test suite makes a product unbuildable by the loop
incidents.rule: A loop CAN correctly diagnose its own blocker and still be structurally unable to fix it if the fix touches a policy only the operator owns - so when a team stalls, READ ITS PLANNER'S NOTES FIRST. If a suite approaches the per-step timeout, the product is unbuildable by the loop; fix the SUITE, and put the fix in a config all call sites inherit.
incidents.signature: One team consistently fails while sibling teams on the same infrastructure ship normally. Every failed engineer and tester attempt log is a 48-byte 'timed out' stub. Shrinking the spec does not help.

incidents.title: A monotonically growing required-reading file silently kills the loop
incidents.rule: Any file injected into EVERY iteration's prompt is a resource. Bound it by CHARACTERS, not item count, and cap it at write time. A monotonically growing steering artifact will silently kill the loop on the same timeout cap; when it does, the log looks exactly like a rate-limit stall - distinguish by content, not size.
incidents.signature: Same log signature as INC-0002, but the guilty artifact is a required-reading file (a roadmap, a design doc, a large context file) that grew organically over many iterations.

incidents.title: A killed step with no verdict token is read as REVERTED
incidents.rule: A machine-parsed verdict token that defaults to the destructive answer on absence is a critical safety hazard when its writer runs under a hard timeout. Write the verdict EARLY on decisive evidence only, budget verification to the cap, and treat lower-priority audits as follow-ups.
incidents.signature: An iteration passes every gate, tests are green, git status is clean - and the loop reverts anyway with no error message. The final step's log ends mid-verification.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - the verdict parser and the release-gate role card that this incident is about: `parse_ship_action` in `foundry.py` accepts only PUSHED/REVERTED and returns None otherwise, and `roles/final.md` carries the verify-first exception that forbids this one role from checkpointing its verdict.

incidents.title: Checkpoint-first: a killed step that already wrote its output still counts
incidents.rule: Success is an ARTIFACT, not an exit code. Under a hard timeout, an agent that writes its minimal complete output first and refines in place still succeeds if killed. Correspondingly: never call a timeout a failure without checking whether the output file exists.
incidents.signature: An attempt log is 48 bytes ('timed out after 600s') and the loop treats the iteration as a success anyway - because the OUTPUT FILE exists.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - the write-early contract lives in the `roles/*.md` cards, which are read from disk per run, and the success-is-an-artifact rule is enforced by the stage runner rather than by exit code.

incidents.title: Diagnose stalled work from the duration distribution, not the outcome
incidents.rule: A success predicate defined as 'the output file exists' hides a chronically over-budget step. Report the DURATION DISTRIBUTION per step, not just the outcome, and compare against a sibling running the same pipeline on the same box - which cheaply falsifies 'the machine is slow' or 'the provider is throttling'.
incidents.signature: The loop's per-step success rate looks healthy. But if you compute the median wall-clock per step, one specific step sits AT the hard cap.

incidents.title: Stale IPC endpoint after the host application restarts
incidents.rule: A subprocess spawned with no explicit env inherits every environmental identifier the parent captured at launch - including socket paths tied to a PID that can change. When the parent long outlives its environmental assumptions, resolve identifiers at spawn time with an ACTIVE probe (connect, not exists). Never trust a PID from a filename against PID reuse.
incidents.signature: Every step instantly fails (same-second timing, not a timeout). Attempt logs are ~500 bytes containing CLI help text ('did not match ... check syntax'), not the timeout string. The process looks alive.

incidents.title: Interactive-only credential expiry silently stalls unattended loops
incidents.rule: Any long unattended loop depending on a human-refreshable credential will eventually stall on expiry, not throttle. Watch the LONG-LIVED credential (12h class), not the short-lived derivative one, and pair a 'time-remaining' alarm with a log-string alarm - each catches what the other misses.
incidents.signature: Step logs say 'credential refresh failed' or 'authentication timed out'. Distinct from throttle ('service is busy') and from the hard timeout ('timed out after 600s'). The lead thread also stalls, so hours can pass silently.

incidents.title: Sleep beats the wake-lock on battery power
incidents.rule: A wake-lock utility on a laptop is not enough on battery power - the 'prevent system sleep' primitive is often silently gated on AC. Before an overnight unattended run, plug in AC and confirm the OS assertion is actually held. If the machine sleeps, retry-and-backoff cannot save you.
incidents.signature: Every task fails with the same 'Connection stalled - no data received for 120 s (network issue or system sleep)' error. Retry-and-backoff works correctly and still cannot win.

incidents.title: Concurrent agent brains silently starve and kill each other
incidents.rule: Multiple agents share a model-provider quota, and the losing brain cannot degrade gracefully - it dies silently. Before ANY batch launch: count the live brains against one account, and if a dispatcher is already alive, either wait for a quiescent window or run inline. Signature: 'connection stalled 120s' plus 'service busy' on multiple tasks with confirmed AC power.
incidents.signature: Multiple tasks fail with 'Connection stalled - no data received for 120 s' plus occasional 'service is busy'. AC power is confirmed. A long-running dispatcher process is alive.

incidents.title: A loop's `git add -A` sweeps a human's uncommitted edits into a loop commit
incidents.rule: The git index is process-shared. A blanket `git add -A` stages everything in the tree, including uncommitted work you did not author. When a loop is live: do not hand-edit its tree; if you must, drop the loop's STOP sentinel first. A path-limited commit protects the loop from you, not you from the loop. `commit -a` sweeps too: commit named paths only.
incidents.signature: `git log --oneline -S "<a phrase you typed>" -- <file>` shows your text landed in a commit whose SUBJECT is the loop's story.

incidents.title: add-then-commit is a shared-index race; use a path-limited commit
incidents.rule: The git index is process-shared: a pathless commit takes whatever is staged at that instant, not what you staged. For any out-of-band write to a repo another writer touches: name the paths on the commit itself (`git commit -m 'msg' -- <paths>`) rather than doing add-then-commit. Do not force-push while the loop is live.
incidents.signature: You ran `git add <paths>` followed by a separate `git commit` and the resulting commit contains files you never touched. Diff against your parent shows the loop's whole iteration.

incidents.title: A revert-on-failure loop destroys uncommitted human work in a shared tree
incidents.rule: A loop's revert-to-remote cannot distinguish loop dirt from human work-in-progress. Guard shared trees with a per-team STOP sentinel that names owner, files at risk, lift condition and whether restart is needed. Sentinels are polled every round; the enabled flag needs a restart. Verify the lift condition in the SAME command that removes it.
incidents.signature: A loop is enabled that commits from a working directory where another writer has uncommitted changes. The loop's failure path is a full reset to the remote head.

incidents.title: Git identity leak: real name via ambient global config
incidents.rule: For any repo destined to be public, set BOTH repo-local `user.name` AND `user.email` (to a public handle and id-anchored noreply) BEFORE the first commit. Verify with `git log --all --format='%an <%ae>'`. A noreply email alone does not stop the ambient global name from leaking. An `includeIf` gitdir must be the REAL path, not a symlink.
incidents.signature: `git log --all --format='%an <%ae>'` on any repo shows an identity string you did not consciously set for THAT repo.

incidents.title: Anti-delegation clause must forbid 'scaffold a loop' too
incidents.rule: A subagent reads 'do not spawn a nested agent' literally. Forbid every escape hatch by name in the SAME clause: nested agents, scaffolding a loop, writing prd/prompt/progress files, launching detached processes, handing off to a future iteration. Include the clause INLINE, not by reference. Kill an unauthorized loop by removing its required input, not just its pid.
incidents.signature: A subagent instructed to do work returns quickly and successfully, but the expected output file is empty or missing. Meanwhile a new nested loop or a prd.json / prompt.md scaffold appears alongside.

incidents.title: A killed detached loop resurrects with a new PPID
incidents.rule: To stop a well-behaved detached loop, remove the input it polls (a STOP file it honors), not just its pid - a supervisor or scheduler can re-launch a killed pid. Same argv on a new pid = auto-resurrection; different argv = a fresh authorized launch. Hunt the launcher accordingly, and leave a documented STOP so you and the other session do not fight over the process.
incidents.signature: You kill the loop's pid. Later, `ps` shows a fresh pid with ppid 1, running the same loop script, on a new sleep-backoff cycle.

incidents.title: Fail-open detector: pipe alternation matches nothing under one regex flavor
incidents.rule: A negative result from a detector is NOT evidence of health. Every alarm must be proven against a KNOWN-BAD sample before it is trusted (fires) and against a known-good sample (does not fire). Fail-open monitoring is worse than none. And know your regex flavor: `\|` is alternation in BRE but a LITERAL pipe in ripgrep - use plain `|`.
incidents.signature: A monitor built on `grep -E 'A\|B'` or `grep 'A\|B'` prints nothing while the eye clearly sees both patterns in the log. A negative result is being read as health.

incidents.title: Fail-open detector: parsing the wrong column reports healthy
incidents.rule: A parser that fails silently by returning nothing is indistinguishable from a healthy sample. Sanity-check every parser by asserting that its rows come back with PLAUSIBLE values; if every row is unparseable, you have the wrong column, not a healthy system. Never make an alarm's positive answer look like its negative answer.
incidents.signature: A cookie- or config-file parser produces empty output that reads as 'nothing to report' when in fact every row is unparseable because the code is reading the wrong field.

incidents.title: A steering channel counts only when the consumer's own parser emits it
incidents.rule: A steering channel counts as delivered only when the CONSUMER's own parser emits it - verify by calling that parser, not by inspecting the file. Know its rules: item budget, character budget, format markers. Read the limit in the version ACTUALLY RUNNING, not the newest source. Bound anything injected into every prompt by CHARACTERS, cap at write time, and check what survives.
incidents.signature: You wrote the steering text into the right file with the right words. The next iteration's behavior shows no evidence the agent read it.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - the consumer parser is `learnings_digest` in `foundry.py`; the delivery bounds are `PROMPT_LEARNINGS_HEAD_BULLET_CHARS` and `PROMPT_LEARNINGS_HEAD_BUDGET_CHARS`, and the digest emits its own elision notice, which is what makes a dropped steering bullet greppable instead of silent.

incidents.title: Stale module import: 'shipped' is not 'live'
incidents.rule: A long-running process runs the code it imported AT LAUNCH. Merged is not shipped is not live: git can say 'landed' while the process is still on the old bytecode. Ship a live-lag check that compares process start-time against `git log --since` on the imported module. Role/prompt files read per-run ARE live even when the module is frozen - distinguish them. New config semantics need a restart too.
incidents.signature: A long-running dispatcher's uptime is measured in days. `git log --since=<start>` on the module it imported shows dozens of commits since. The behavior on disk does not match what the process seems to be running.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - the dispatcher does a plain `import foundry` once at launch, with no reload primitive and no self-restart.

Second confirmation, 2026-08-15: a live dispatcher with 1d22h uptime was still running the module revision it imported at launch while the repository head had moved on by many commits. Every prompt-budget constant measured from the working tree was therefore the wrong number for the running loop - so a stale module silently invalidates measurements taken about it, not just fixes shipped to it.

incidents.title: Test precondition on gitignored local state passes only on this machine
incidents.rule: A test that reads ambient filesystem state depends on gitignored files a fresh clone does not have. Before asserting on a path, ask whether git tracks it; if not, build the fixture yourself in `tmp_path` instead of asserting on the ambient tree. A test that passes only on this machine is not a test.
incidents.signature: A test passes locally on every developer machine, then fails immediately in a fresh CI clone. The diff between environments is directories or files gitignored by policy.

incidents.title: CI shallow clone breaks tests that read git history
incidents.rule: CI defaults to a depth-1 clone; any test that reads git history sees a different world there. Set `fetch-depth: 0`. Before blaming the commit under test, ask what CI's environment does NOT have: git history, tags, submodules, a TTY, network, timezone, locale. A synthetic depth-1 clone locally reproduces the failure in one step.
incidents.signature: Tests pass locally, fail in CI, and none of them are testing the code under review. The failures reference git-history-shaped values.

incidents.title: Backtick command substitution in a heredoc corrupts and executes
incidents.rule: In an UNQUOTED heredoc, backticks and $() are executed by the shell - both corrupting file content and potentially running arbitrary commands. Use a QUOTED heredoc (`<<'EOF'`) for any write containing code citations, and verify the resulting file for control characters and empty `()` pairs afterwards. And nothing after the terminator on the same line.
incidents.signature: A file written via an UNQUOTED heredoc contains empty `()` where citations should be, has control characters or carriage-return spam, and `wc -l` disagrees wildly with byte size.

incidents.title: Retrying a killed verification step without resumable evidence is one failure, not four chances
incidents.rule: A retry is a second chance only if something carried forward. Under a hard cap, N retries of a deterministic over-budget step is one failure repeated N times. Give the step a place to record partial results, key that record to the exact input state so a stale one is discarded, and keep it OUT of the channel a parser reads as the verdict.
incidents.signature: Every attempt of the same step fails identically, at the same duration, with the same short timeout log. The retry count in the logs looks like resilience, while the outcome is exactly the outcome of one attempt.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - `MAX_ATTEMPTS` and `retry_directive` in `foundry.py` (the retry text states in its own docstring that it deliberately does not read the previous attempt), the verify-first exception in `roles/final.md`, and the pre-ship clone gate whose 'could not complete' exit code is already treated as evidence about the machine rather than the tree - the asymmetry part (3) asks to be generalized.

incidents.title: A whole-batch verification veto turns one bad item into a permanent block
incidents.rule: A gate whose verdict covers the whole batch, and whose caller aborts on any failure, turns one bad item into a permanent block as soon as the queue keeps growing - a ratchet, not a filter. Judge each item on its own evidence, act per item, and never let the gate's exit code re-create the batch veto.
incidents.signature: A gate that used to pass now refuses on every cycle, and it names a DIFFERENT offending item each time. The queue grows monotonically. Each individual refusal is correct and well-reported.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - commit af2db9a makes quote verification per record so one bad quote cannot veto the pool; a747cc8 adds the verified-staging directory so bounding a pass stays honest; tools/verify_quotes.py documents why --partition exists in its own module docstring.

incidents.title: A cache keyed on a recycled id judged each record on its predecessor's evidence
incidents.rule: Never key derived evidence on an identifier a rejection can recycle: 'next free' ids are unique only among ACCEPTED records. Before believing a mass verdict, count its DISTINCT reasons - one identical reason across hundreds of inputs indicts the judge, not the data. Always re-run a gate on the full population; a hand-labelled sample finds only the false positives it contains.
incidents.signature: A mass verdict whose stated reason is IDENTICAL across hundreds of distinct inputs. Runtime is also far higher than it should be, because the cache is not actually caching anything.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - commit 315bc6e adds the interchangeable-detector refusal this gate implements; tools/promote.py holds the fixture comparison and the ranking helper.

incidents.title: When two distributions overlap there is no threshold - change the signal, not the number
incidents.rule: Before choosing a threshold, measure the MINIMUM of one population against the MAXIMUM of the other. If they overlap, no cutoff exists and tuning only picks which error you make - find an EXECUTABLE consequence of the two things being the same instead. Require mutual agreement (one-way is subsumption) and test the silent half, or any broad check counts as a twin.
incidents.signature: Every candidate cutoff either misses real positives or refuses real work, and moving it just trades one error for the other. Each individual measurement looks reasonable.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - commit 315bc6e ships the behavioural interchangeability check that replaced the lexical threshold; e37ef89 and tools/verify_mutations.py are the mutation harness that found the blind spots.

incidents.title: When a check reports missing content, the extractor is the first suspect
incidents.rule: When a check reports missing content, suspect the extractor before the artifact: a false negative about content points at a destructive remedy. Count the units two ways (strict pattern versus loose structural) and let disagreement indict the measurement. Read the real format off disk before writing any repair, and never grade delegated work by a runner's success ledger.
incidents.signature: The reported-missing content forms a clean PREFIX plus SUFFIX of the whole, instead of being scattered through the middle. Two different ways of counting the same units disagree.

incidents.title: Rewriting a region by slicing between two markers deletes whatever else lives there
incidents.rule: Never rewrite a file region by slicing between two found markers: the slice is defined by position, so it silently deletes whatever else sits in the gap. Use an anchored replace whose anchor is asserted to occur exactly once, and after any slice edit diff against the last known-good revision - 'N insertions, 0 deletions' is the proof.
incidents.signature: A tool that worked stops working immediately after an edit you believe was confined to one region, raising NameError or AttributeError for a symbol you never touched. The file still parses.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - tools/promote.py, whose _rank helper sat between the two anchors and was deleted and then restored verbatim.

incidents.title: A concurrency test with no forced interleaving passes loudest when the feature is absent
incidents.rule: A test of an emergent property (locking, coalescing, dedup, cache hits, backpressure) must assert its own PRECONDITION - that the interleaving really happened - or it is greenest when the mechanism is absent. Force the window, assert on the field that races, mutation-verify each defect against a NAMED test, and run the checker from two working directories.
incidents.signature: A test for an emergent property - locking, coalescing, deduplication, cache hits, backpressure - is green, and stays green when you delete the mechanism it exists to test.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - e37ef89 and tools/verify_mutations.py implement the plant-one-defect-at-a-time harness this fix prescribes, with restoration verified by content in a finally block.

incidents.title: Removing a veto exposes the broken classifier it was masking
incidents.rule: A blocking gate upstream of a classifier hides that classifier's errors, so removing the gate does not create the refusals you then see - it reveals them. Treat the first batch of refusals after unblocking as unverified, hand-check them against the primary source, and re-run the repaired check over the historical verdicts before letting any of them stand.
incidents.signature: You remove a blocking aggregate gate expecting a flood of passes, and get a small number of confident, specific refusals instead. Each surviving refusal is individually plausible and quotable - which is exactly why you believe it.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - the normaliser repair in `tools/verify_quotes.py` (71c46ad) landed only after the whole-batch veto was removed (af2db9a), and that order is what made the false accusations visible at all.

incidents.title: One normaliser is not enough if it maps the two sides into different conventions
incidents.rule: One normaliser on both sides is not enough - it must map both sides into the SAME convention. A rule right for one input (tags become spaces) is corruption on an input that never had tags. Prove a comparison with a known-GOOD pair as well as a known-bad one, and when a checker accuses an artifact you can see is correct, suspect the checker: a fail-closed defect points at a destructive repair.
incidents.signature: A checker reports that a string is absent from a document where you can see it with your own eyes. The near-miss it prints is a clean prefix or suffix of the real text, or differs from it only in whitespace or punctuation.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - the space-before-punctuation collapse added inside the single `_norm` in `tools/verify_quotes.py`, with the two prior recurrences recorded in the same module's history.

incidents.title: A malformed item aborts the per-item pass, and the crash reinstates the veto wearing a traceback
incidents.rule: Per-item isolation lives in the error path, not the loop. A for-loop makes the WORK per item; only a per-item catch makes the FAILURES per item, and an uncaught exception is a batch-wide verdict however granular the loop. Validate each item's shape, quarantine a bad one with a reason, and test that good items in the SAME batch still get through.
incidents.signature: The pass that was supposed to judge items one at a time dies with a type error naming one item, and nothing is promoted. The log reads as an unrelated bug rather than as a policy decision, so the outcome is never recognised as the failure you just eliminated.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - the record-shape gate added alongside the per-record partition mode in `tools/verify_quotes.py`, so a malformed candidate is quarantined instead of crashing the pass.

incidents.title: Two individually safe options are unsafe together when their combination leaves a consumer unable to distinguish two states
incidents.rule: Ask of any two individually safe options whether their COMBINATION leaves a consumer unable to distinguish two states. A per-run bound plus an in-place 'done' marker is the canonical pair: the bound makes 'all of these were checked' false, and the in-place marker deletes the evidence of which ones were. Make the checked set a separate LOCATION, and make any bound visible in the artifact.
incidents.signature: Two changes, each reviewed and each safe. Nothing in either diff is wrong. The defect exists only in the state the pair produces, and it shows up as a consumer reading a collection whose members no longer all mean the same thing.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - the `--verified` staging destination (a747cc8), added so that bounding a verification pass and promoting from it stay honest at the same time.

incidents.title: A relaunch that bypasses the canonical launcher runs healthy but unobservable, and the diagnostic inverts
incidents.rule: A launcher script is often part of the observability contract, not a convenience. Reproducing its command without its environment yields a process that works and cannot be seen, and every log-reading check then reports a failure that did not happen. Relaunch through the canonical entry point, and verify a restart by asserting the artifact your diagnostics read, not that the process exists.
incidents.signature: The process is alive with the right parent and the right arguments, but the log has no launch banner, and every freshness or liveness check that reads that log reports a problem. Restarting again reproduces the same silence.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - `launch_dispatcher.sh`, the dispatcher's own stdout redirection, and the `live-lag` verb that reads the launch banner out of the log.

incidents.title: A liveness check built on a process-table grep counts itself
incidents.rule: A process-table grep counts itself - the measuring command's arguments contain the search term, so a 'something is running' check is never false. Use a matcher that excludes its own process, and prove any busy/idle check TWO-SIDED: zero when nothing runs, non-zero with one known worker. A check never seen returning false has not been tested.
incidents.signature: A 'something is running' check is never false. The measured count is exactly one more than the truth, and it reads one at moments when you know for certain that nothing is running.

incidents.title: A determinism test that scans the live working tree cannot pass while another writer edits it
incidents.rule: Determinism is a property of a function over a FIXED input. A test that scans the live working tree twice and compares is really asserting that no other writer touched the tree, so it tests the writers, not the code - and it passes in isolation, which reads as flakiness. Give the test a fixture it owns, or snapshot the input once and assert the snapshot is unchanged.
incidents.signature: A test asserting that two consecutive runs produce identical output fails in the full suite and passes in isolation. The failure moves between runs and correlates with another session's file timestamps rather than with anything that changed under test.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - the scan-determinism tests that take the repository root itself as their scan target, so the fixture is the live mutable checkout.

incidents.title: A budget is not a sample: a sorted head is a permanent filter, disguised as a performance knob
incidents.rule: For ANY truncated pass, ask whether the ORDER is independent of the PROPERTY being measured. Filename, insertion, directory and id order almost never are - so a sorted head is a permanent filter wearing a performance knob's clothes. Round-robin across the dimension you care about, best-first inside each bucket, and give unclassifiable items their own bucket.
incidents.signature: A bounded pass reports steady healthy throughput, but its OUTPUT is concentrated in one region of the input space - and that region is the one that sorts first.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-gap-radar - tools/verify_quotes.py, function select_bounded, whose docstring records the measured distribution and why the previous sorted-head selection was a bias rather than a sample.

incidents.title: A guard that asserts a lifecycle stage fails at exactly the moment it was written to protect
incidents.rule: Write down the state your guard FORBIDS, then ask whether the project intends to REACH that state. If it does, the guard is asserting a schedule, not a safety property, and it will fail precisely when the guarded event happens. The invariant worth protecting sits one level down: not 'no remote' but 'no credential in a remote'.
incidents.signature: A safety test has never once failed, and the state it forbids is a state on the project's own roadmap. It fails for the first time immediately after a milestone.

incidents.title: A verifier that lived and answered can still deliver an unusable verdict
incidents.rule: A verifier that answers is not a verifier that reported: transport AND the stored log can truncate at the same boundary, losing the finding entirely. Have the verifier write its full report to a FILE and reply with only the verdict table. A summary line asserting a count is a claim about findings, not a finding - never quote a partial trace as a result.
incidents.signature: A verifier reports a COUNT of failures in its summary line but the detail for the failing item is missing, and re-reading the stored log truncates at the same place.

incidents.title: Self-review does not catch recurrences of your own documented rules
incidents.rule: Self-review is graded by the context that produced the defect, so a rule can be perfectly known and still not applied - knowing and executing are different capabilities. Use an independent verifier with access to the artifact and primary sources but NOT your reasoning, and treat a recurrence as evidence about the enforcement point, never as a reason to reword the rule.
incidents.signature: An artifact passes its author's careful self-review, and an independent pass immediately finds defects that match rules the author can quote from memory.

incidents.title: An anchored replace that matches a PREFIX of a line is still 'exactly once'
incidents.rule: An anchor that is a PREFIX of the real line still matches 'exactly once', so a uniqueness assertion certifies ambiguity and never completeness - anchor on the whole line or include its terminator. In a shared appended structure never assume the next sequential symbol name is free: read the live file and history, and assert AFTER writing that each symbol is defined exactly once.
incidents.signature: An edit asserted to match exactly once succeeds, and afterwards the file contains a duplicated fragment of the line you replaced - or one symbol defined twice, the later definition shadowing the earlier.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-failure-modes - this repository is where the collision happened: tools/corpus.py now carries the repaired composition line, and commit bccb9d1 is the concurrent writer's batch that was briefly shadowed.

incidents.title: Pushing a local repository to a new remote publishes its whole history, not its current tree
incidents.rule: Pushing an existing repository publishes its HISTORY. Before the first push audit every path ever tracked, every blob version and every commit message, never only the tree, and install a pre-push guard that scans the pushed range. Excluding a file from the tree does not remove it from history.
incidents.signature: A repository is about to be pushed for the first time, the plan is stated in terms of which files to exclude, and nobody has listed the paths that were EVER tracked.

incidents.title: Disabling a loop's push while its failure path resets to the remote erases shipped work
incidents.rule: Before turning off a pipeline's publish or push step, find what its rollback resets TO. If rollback targets the published state, publishing is part of the durability contract, not an optional gate.
incidents.signature: A proposal simplifies a pipeline by turning off its publish step, while the rollback path of the same pipeline hard-resets to the published state and never fetches.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - the loop engine whose failure path reverts with a hard reset to the remote branch, the behaviour this near miss depended on. The failure was a design draft that was caught; it did not occur in that repository.

incidents.title: A script with external writes was only dry-run for its first step, and only write-last ordering made its failure harmless
incidents.rule: In any script that writes externally, order every fallible local step first and every external write last, and dry-run the WHOLE script end to end against scratch copies before the real run, not just its hardest step.
incidents.signature: A multi-step script that pushes or resets exits non-zero partway through its first real run, having only been rehearsed on its hardest step.

incidents.title: In an ordered replacement list, a general rule placed before a specific one consumes its match
incidents.rule: In ordered rewrite lists (sed scripts, replacement files, routing tables) put specific rules before general ones, and verify on the OUTPUT, not on the rules.
incidents.signature: A replacement list gains a broad pattern at the top, above a narrower pattern for a case the broad one also matches.

incidents.title: Citing an identifier in the same parallel tool block that creates it makes the citation a guess
incidents.rule: Never cite an identifier produced by a step that has not returned yet. If call B needs a value from call A, B goes in a later block and quotes what A actually returned.
incidents.signature: One batch of parallel tool calls contains both a step that creates an identifier (commit hash, ticket number, file path) and a step that quotes it.

incidents.title: A cached credential made a dependency look optional, and the outage was filed under the wrong root cause
incidents.rule: A dependency that 'works without' its credential may be riding a cache. Prove independence by checking the whole credential chain's expiry, not by one success, and do not file a root cause until the cache lifetime is accounted for.
incidents.signature: After an outage a component works although its documented credential is known to be expired, and the conclusion drawn is that the credential is not needed.
evidence: https://github.com/jeffma8888/agent-foundry - the loop engine whose credential exporter and stage failures this describes.

incidents.title: Bundling safe local steps with an approval-gated step loses the local steps when the gate refuses
incidents.rule: Never bundle unattended-safe steps with a step that needs a human's approval. Split the chain at the approval boundary so a refusal costs only the gated step.
incidents.signature: A single shell command performs an edit, a commit and a push, and the push is subject to a per-call human approval rule.

incidents.title: A fallible edit script followed by a semicolon let the commit run on a partial result
incidents.rule: Validate all preconditions before the first write, and never let a later step run after an earlier one failed: join dependent steps with a short-circuit and, not a semicolon.
incidents.signature: A script that writes several files is followed by a commit joined with a semicolon, and the script's output contains a traceback.

incidents.title: A hygiene rule written against surface syntax rejects valid cases; enforce the property at the boundary where it happens
incidents.rule: Enforce a property where it happens (the network boundary), not by banning the syntax that usually precedes it. Before adopting a hygiene rule, run it against the features the project must test and ask what valid input it would reject.
incidents.signature: A rule meant to guarantee a behaviour (no network calls) is phrased as a ban on a syntactic form (no URL literals), and the code under test legitimately handles that form.

incidents.title: A command-line agent silently ran an older model than assumed and ignored an explicit model override
incidents.rule: A model setting is verified only by the model ID in the response metadata. A flag that is accepted is not a flag that took effect, and a tool that falls back instead of failing makes every override unverifiable until you read the metadata.
incidents.signature: A model setting is accepted without error, the tool answers normally, and nobody has read the model identifier from the response metadata.

incidents.title: A display name drifted from the model identifier it was supposed to describe
incidents.rule: Record the exact model ID wherever a model is credited, and derive the display name from it. A display name is not evidence of which model did the work.
incidents.signature: Credits, rosters or reports carry a hand-typed model name next to an identifier that was typed separately.

incidents.title: A scope cut was mapped against the previous version of its baseline document
incidents.rule: Before mapping against a baseline document, read its current version and commit from disk and write that commit into the header of the derived document.
incidents.signature: A derived document cites a baseline by version label only, and the baseline has changed since the author last read it.

incidents.title: Test seams declared from memory carried wrong field names, and a bulk replacement silently missed a row
incidents.rule: Search for every identifier you put into a test oracle; never declare a seam from memory. Make each bulk replacement assert its expected match count.
incidents.signature: A test oracle or interface section lists identifiers that nobody has searched for in the design, and the document has had bulk edits applied by script.

incidents.title: A revision that closed every finding introduced new defects in the seams it added
incidents.rule: An accepted finding is not a closed finding. Re-verify every new concrete claim a fix introduces against its source of truth before declaring the finding closed.
incidents.signature: Each review round's fix adds new concrete claims (types, hooks, signatures), and the next round's findings are mostly about those additions.

incidents.title: A broad exception handler hid the difference between 'not found' and 'unknown name'
incidents.rule: When one error type subclasses another, order handlers narrow to broad and test the exact type. A broad assertion is green for every cause beneath it.
incidents.signature: A handler catches a parent exception type first, and a sibling error with a different meaning is a subclass of it.

incidents.title: A 'client too old' error was assumed to be client-side; the gate was on the server and keyed on the request body
incidents.rule: Before working around a version or access error, find where the check lives. A server-side gate on client identity is a decision for the human who owns the access, never something to strip or fake.
incidents.signature: A vendor coding CLI says a newer version is required for a feature, and the working theory is a local version check.

incidents.title: A probe hung on a background child that held the pipe, and the timeout wrapper it relied on did not exist
incidents.rule: Never background a long-lived process inside a captured pipeline, and confirm every wrapper command exists on the target OS before relying on it. Read the error stream before theorising about the hang.
incidents.signature: A shell one-liner starts a long-lived server with a trailing background marker inside a captured pipeline, and wraps the client in a timeout command.

incidents.title: Exhaustive test wording created expectations the design never defined
incidents.rule: A per-ID test oracle may only require values its source of truth defines. 'Every' in a test requirement needs a check that the source covers every member.
incidents.signature: A test requirement says 'every' member of a set, and the source of truth defines behaviour for only some of them.

incidents.title: A reviewer's claim about framework behaviour was wrong, and accepting it would have put a wrong assertion into the tests
incidents.rule: A reviewer's statement about framework or library behaviour is a hypothesis with the same standing as the author's. Verify it at the pinned version, reading the whole function, before it changes a test or a design.
incidents.signature: A review finding states what a library or framework does, in confident terms, and the proposed change follows directly from that statement.

incidents.title: A spec that tightened validation before the data migration made every real-data test fail
incidents.rule: When a spec tightens validation, order the data migration before the code, or give the implementer an explicit scratch-copy check, so code defects and missing data are tested separately.
incidents.signature: A new spec makes a field required, while the step that adds that field to the existing data is scheduled after the code.

incidents.title: A launcher pointed a live unattended loop at the development checkout instead of a pinned release
incidents.rule: A running unattended loop executes a pinned, tagged copy of every tool it calls, never a tree someone is editing. Make upgrades an explicit step, not a side effect of a commit.
incidents.signature: The path a production loop uses to call its stage engine is the same working tree where developers are still making changes.

incidents.title: A 'graceful' stop flag checked before every stage would have discarded the in-flight iteration's finished work
incidents.rule: Before using a stop flag to drain a loop, read every place it is checked, and set it only after the last check that would discard work.
incidents.signature: A stop sentinel is meant to drain a loop between iterations, but nobody has checked where in the loop it is read.

incidents.title: A worker's end-of-run cleanup deleted a shared scratch directory, taking the coordinator's live watcher and its log with it
incidents.rule: Delete only the files you created, by name, never a parent directory you were pointed at; a successful create-parents call says nothing about ownership. Give each worker its own scratch subdirectory, never run a live control process from shared temp space, and report every delete.
incidents.signature: Two agents are told to use the same scratch directory, and one of them finishes by deleting the directory recursively.

incidents.title: An operator directive was visible to the planner but no rule ranked it, so it was deferred while the loop shipped its own picks
incidents.rule: A directive to an agent system needs a route into the decision, not only visibility. Before queuing one, read the picker's prompt and confirm which rule will select it; if none does, write that rule first.
incidents.signature: A directive is placed in the file every role reads first, and the planning role's output acknowledges it and then does something else.

incidents.title: A retry ladder wrapped the model call but not the credential helper on the same path, so one helper blip became a long hold
incidents.rule: A retry ladder must cover every external call on the path to a model turn, including helpers that fetch credentials. When a dependency that passes manual probes fails in the loop, log the failing attempt's stderr instead of a classification, and never let a one-shot preflight decide whether an unattended system restarts.
incidents.signature: A credential helper that passes every manual probe exits non-zero about once an hour inside the loop, and the loop reports an expired session.

incidents.title: A gate compared the candidate commit with itself because a local clone redefines the remote-tracking ref
incidents.rule: A check that runs inside a clone must not rely on remote-tracking refs. State the baseline commit explicitly, and reproduce the ref topology in a scratch repo before trusting the check.
incidents.signature: A check diffs against the main branch of the remote, and it runs in a fresh clone of a local checkout rather than of the real remote.

incidents.title: Two reviewers' table parsers undercounted rows on escaped pipes and a sum included a header
incidents.rule: Parse table syntax properly before reporting a count, and cross-check any count or sum against a second method before it reaches a verdict.
incidents.signature: A count or sum of table rows comes from splitting lines on the column delimiter, and some cells contain the delimiter escaped.

incidents.title: A plan claimed minutes-denominated stage times fit inside a cap stated in seconds
incidents.rule: Convert every budget and estimate to one unit before writing that one fits inside the other.
incidents.signature: A budget in one unit is compared with an estimate in another, and the document states that one fits inside the other.

incidents.title: Four different fetch failures were all reported as 'the site blocks automated access'
incidents.rule: Never report 'the site blocks automated access' from a fetch-tool error. Name the failure class first: client error, redirect loop (cookies), form token, or a challenge page. Only a challenge page or an explicit policy is a real block, and the answer to it is an official API or another source, not a disguise.
incidents.signature: A fetch returns a connection error, a redirect error or a 403, and the agent's next sentence says the site 'blocks automated access' without naming which of those it was.

incidents.title: A bundled retry worked and the fix was credited to 'looking like a normal browser', which was wrong in every case tested
incidents.rule: When a bundled retry works, isolate the variable before naming the fix: a 200 confirms the bundle, not your story. Read robots.txt before retrying a site that refused, stop on a disallow, and treat a challenge page as a refusal: use an official API or hand the user the link.
incidents.signature: Several changes go into one retry (new client, new User-Agent, cookie jar, form handling), the retry succeeds, and the summary names the change the agent expected to matter.

incidents.title: A brief named a source directory the repository does not have, written from a conventional layout instead of a listing
incidents.rule: Write path rules in a brief from a listing taken when the brief is written, never from memory of a conventional layout.
incidents.signature: A brief scopes work to a directory by name, and the name is the conventional one for the language or framework rather than one anyone listed.

incidents.title: Tests and code were written against a spec before its independent review returned, and the rulings then changed
incidents.rule: An independent spec review is a gate, not a parallel track. Keep idle teammates busy with work that does not depend on the spec's open rulings.
incidents.signature: Downstream roles start in parallel with the independent review of the document they depend on, to keep everyone busy.

incidents.title: A teammate's write boundary contradicted the charter's file layout, so a required record landed where activation would reject it
incidents.rule: Derive a teammate's write boundary from the governing charter's layout, and check the two agree before sending the brief.
incidents.signature: A brief limits writes to one directory, and the governing charter requires an output in a different one.

incidents.title: Keeping an error prefix did not keep the downstream classification, and a free-text reason could carry markers or secrets
incidents.rule: When output feeds a downstream classifier, test the classifier's verdict on it, not its prefix. Emit fixed categories instead of free text when the text could carry secrets or markers.
incidents.signature: New text is appended to a log line that a downstream classifier scans, on the argument that the line keeps its prefix.

incidents.title: A subprocess wrapper decoded output strictly, so malformed bytes skipped the retry and redaction path
incidents.rule: Put transport decoding inside the same failure boundary as the call, and test the boundary with a real process emitting malformed bytes, not only fakes returning clean text.
incidents.signature: A wrapper runs an external command with strict text decoding, and every test feeds it clean strings.

incidents.title: A second writer reused a shared registry's batch name and its entries silently vanished
incidents.rule: Before adding to a shared registry, read the current last value of every identifier kind you will create (record IDs, batch names, keys), not only the record ID.
incidents.signature: Two writers extend one registry and pick the next batch name from their own expectation of what is next.

incidents.title: Two writers used the same short question ID for different gaps, so a real gap looked ruled
incidents.rule: Give every shared ID a namespace one writer owns, such as the row or author; a bare short name is a collision waiting to happen.
incidents.signature: A shared question table uses short bare names, and several writers add questions without a namespace.

incidents.title: Reviewers and QA wrote absolute home paths and notes paths into repository docs, and only the push guard caught them
incidents.rule: Tell authors how to cite private material in the brief, and keep the leak scan as a pre-push gate rather than the only control.
incidents.signature: Documents authored by several agents cite local files by absolute path or by the location of private lead notes.

incidents.title: An absence check passed vacuously because the forbidden text never matched the real title and the document may never have been read
incidents.rule: Every absence assertion needs a positive control from the same read, and matching must be substring-tolerant of the real data shape.
incidents.signature: A test asserts a string occurs zero times in a page, and the count is zero for reasons unrelated to the page content.

incidents.title: Controls that fail in only one direction, a drop guard keyed on a name pattern, and refusal tests satisfied by unrelated connection errors
incidents.rule: A control counts only if it fails in both directions; scope destructive guards to recorded identities, and assert the specific refusal, not any error.
incidents.signature: Refusal tests pass against a stub that accepts everything, or against a guard that does nothing because the target is unreachable anyway.

incidents.title: Test-summary assertions broke on ANSI color codes, and compile caches were mistaken for resource leaks
incidents.rule: Normalize terminal output before matching it, and define what counts as an owned resource before counting leaks.
incidents.signature: A test asserts on tool summary text that contains color escape codes, or a leak check counts cache files.

incidents.title: A helper owned by one test root was imported by later roots, creating an undeclared dependency
incidents.rule: Record the owner of every shared helper, and treat an import from another root as a declared dependency.
incidents.signature: A shared helper lives under one row or root and other rows import it without declaring the dependency.

incidents.title: After a dependency fix, two rows still called the same seed function with different payloads
incidents.rule: Verify the call site and arguments, not only the function name, after a dependency change.
incidents.signature: A fix is verified by name, but the same seed function is called with different arguments elsewhere.

incidents.title: An import-level audit missed helper calls that needed a later row, and only the engineer stop rule caught it
incidents.rule: Pair static audits with a stop rule so an engineer halts when a call needs later-row behavior.
incidents.signature: A helper call such as a registered-resource lookup needs a feature delivered by a later row.

incidents.title: QA helpers assumed REST field shapes that differ from the design, and integration files mutated shared state without restoring it
incidents.rule: Every file that mutates shared state restores it or reseeds, and helpers match the documented field shapes.
incidents.signature: Helpers read fields in a shape the design does not use; a spec passes alone and fails after a file that left state changed.

incidents.title: A QA question claimed a credential or fact was undefined when the cut already defined it, and a restore through a gated write needed a satisfying seed
incidents.rule: Search the oracle before recording a question, and design seeds for the gates that tests pass through.
incidents.signature: A recorded question says a value is undefined, but a search of the cut finds it.

incidents.title: Type-stripping rejected TypeScript parameter properties, and admin selectors were undefined
incidents.rule: Write test code in erasable TypeScript only, and assert through contracts that exist.
incidents.signature: A page object fails to load under a type-stripping runtime, or a test needs UI selectors that do not exist.

incidents.title: Teammate replies arrived while the lead was busy and were missed, leaving finished work idle for about 30 minutes
incidents.rule: Verify the last speaker per teammate instead of assuming no news means work is running.
incidents.signature: A teammate finished and replied, but the lead assumed work was still in flight.

incidents.title: A whole-group termination grace period was shorter than the wrapper process, so the wrapper exit ended the wait early
incidents.rule: Bind a group shutdown wait to the group, not to a wrapper that can exit first.
incidents.signature: A shutdown waits for a process group, but the wait ends when the wrapper process exits.

incidents.title: A smoke-run deadline shared the normal step budget policy
incidents.rule: Give runs with different deadline purposes their own policy.
incidents.signature: One timeout policy covers both quick steps and a long smoke run.

incidents.title: macOS sandbox-exec refused to exec a setuid binary, so a sandboxed acceptance profile failed on the process-introspection tool
incidents.rule: List every binary a fixture executes, setuid ones included, when writing a sandbox profile.
incidents.signature: A sandboxed run fails when a fixture runs ps or another setuid tool.

incidents.title: Port validation tests lacked separate absent, zero and shared-port negatives and a positive callback control
incidents.rule: One negative per rejection reason, and a positive control in the same flow.
incidents.signature: One combined negative case passes for any of several unrelated reasons.

incidents.title: Browser-context isolation was mistaken for seed-state isolation
incidents.rule: Isolate each kind of state separately: browser state by context, data by reset and seed.
incidents.signature: A spec reads seed data while relying on a fresh browser context.

incidents.title: URL guards did not prove a test owned the disposable cluster, and shared state was not restored on failure
incidents.rule: Ownership comes from what the test created; restoration belongs in teardown that runs on failure.
incidents.signature: A test destroys or mutates state after checking only that the URL looks safe.

incidents.title: An acyclic declared dependency graph hid producer rows that an acceptance file needed
incidents.rule: An acyclic graph is necessary but not sufficient; derive edges from what each file requires.
incidents.signature: The dependency graph validates, yet an acceptance file needs a row that is not listed.

incidents.title: A test reassignment written only in prose was not enforced by any tool
incidents.rule: Put a reassignment in one registry that every enforcing tool reads.
incidents.signature: A rule about which row owns a test exists in text, and tools disagree or ignore it.

incidents.title: A new test file was placed in a row whose activation order did not include a collection the file creates, and an oracle was asserted without its spec sentence
incidents.rule: Place tests by activation order and quote the spec before asserting.
incidents.signature: A test creates a collection or relies on a rule that the row order or spec does not support.

incidents.title: A later row overwrote a file that was already active
incidents.rule: Active files are append-only; later parts get new destinations.
incidents.signature: Part of a file must activate later, and activating it replaces the active file.

incidents.title: A success control that forbade every connection pinned an implementation from before a later startup step that must connect
incidents.rule: Write prohibitions against the full startup contract, not the current implementation.
incidents.signature: A control test forbids all connections while a later row adds a startup step that connects.

incidents.title: A teammate could not run a destructive git command even when the lead instructed it
incidents.rule: Plan destructive operations for the context that holds the permission.
incidents.signature: A lead instructs a teammate to run a reset or similar, and the permission ceiling refuses it.

incidents.title: A process-group kill test used single-process stubs, so signalling the leader and the group looked the same
incidents.rule: A group-kill test needs a descendant, or it cannot tell group from leader.
incidents.signature: A group-kill test passes with stubs that have no descendants.

incidents.title: A function signature named in the plan but never called by any test shipped ignoring its second argument
incidents.rule: Every planned parameter needs a test that makes it matter.
incidents.signature: The plan names a parameter that no test exercises.

incidents.title: Deleting PostgreSQL environment variables left client tools free to fall back to default host and port
incidents.rule: Pin the target explicitly; do not rely on removing the alternatives.
incidents.signature: A test clears PG variables to avoid the shared cluster, and a client tool uses its defaults.

incidents.title: A timeout override was not re-checked against the newest ruling, and fixes were verified from the coverage note
incidents.rule: Verify from the code line, not from the note that describes it.
incidents.signature: A revision lands after a ruling and keeps an override that the ruling changed.

incidents.title: A fail-closed URL rule copied into several helpers was not applied to every copy or every URL part
incidents.rule: One rule, every copy, every URL part.
incidents.signature: One helper checks the host and another omits the database or port.

incidents.title: A UI test was accepted although no plan row owned a custom UI component it needed
incidents.rule: Every component a test needs has an owning row.
incidents.signature: A test drives a component that no row builds, so the last row meets a missing UI.

incidents.title: A cross-row test needed setup absent from its own lifecycle, and green was claimed without a fresh-clone setup or a canonical temp directory
incidents.rule: Run from a clean state and compare resolved paths before reporting a pass.
incidents.signature: A test passes in a warm checkout and needs a database or path that the fresh lifecycle never creates.

incidents.title: HTTP-only timeouts were copied from a process-hang pattern without the reason
incidents.rule: An override without a stated reason is not reviewable.
incidents.signature: A timeout override appears in a test where its original cause does not apply.

incidents.title: A control relied on state the test had changed earlier and silently became vacuous
incidents.rule: Place a control in the state it needs, and show it can change.
incidents.signature: A control that depends on a signed-in or seeded state runs after the test changed that state.

incidents.title: A rule set widened by tag survived dropping one tag because only some tags had a planted violation
incidents.rule: Every tag in a rule needs its own planted violation.
incidents.signature: A check covers several tags, and removing one tag leaves the suite green.

incidents.title: A second clone named after the remote held a stale tip and was mistaken for the working checkout
incidents.rule: Never identify a checkout by its folder name.
incidents.signature: Two checkouts exist, and the folder name suggests the wrong one is current.

incidents.title: Rows that point at a relationship target were ordered before the target was registered, tempting stubs or optional fields
incidents.rule: Fix the order, not the contract.
incidents.signature: A row needs a related record that a later row creates.

incidents.title: Two validators enforcing the same rule masked single-file mutations
incidents.rule: Test every layer of a redundant check independently.
incidents.signature: Removing one of two redundant checks leaves the suite green.

incidents.title: Signalling a process group of only zombie members returned a permission error on macOS
incidents.rule: Repeat race-dependent cleanup tests; classify errors by what they mean for the target.
incidents.signature: Cleanup fails intermittently when the group has exited but not been reaped.

incidents.title: A reason regex matched text the test itself injected and missed the reason on the error line
incidents.rule: Anchor a reason match to the error line and keep injected text out of its reach.
incidents.signature: A refusal assertion passes because its pattern matches the test input.

incidents.title: A sandboxed HOME hid tool caches such as package-manager shims
incidents.rule: When replacing HOME, forward every cache the tools need and block fetching.
incidents.signature: A tool works normally and fails once HOME points at a temp directory.

incidents.title: A guard control asserted only exit 0, so a warn-and-pass guard looked like a clean pass
incidents.rule: Check output as well as exit status in a clean-pass control.
incidents.signature: A guard that prints an error but exits 0 passes a control that checks the exit code.

incidents.title: A rule scoped to work after a ruling was applied per commit while one commit held old and new patterns
incidents.rule: Scope a rule by the file, not the commit that carries it.
incidents.signature: One commit contains files that predate the ruling and files that follow it.

incidents.title: A digest present anywhere in a manifest was taken as proof it belonged to its file
incidents.rule: Verify pairs, not membership.
incidents.signature: A check finds the digest somewhere in the manifest and passes.

incidents.title: After activation a registry line named a pending path that no longer existed, and a verifier flagged it
incidents.rule: A verifier must follow moves through history, not require the old path to exist.
incidents.signature: A verifier reports a missing path that was legitimately moved at activation.

incidents.title: A poll timeout placed in assertion options was still a propagation override, and shared helpers were left out of the dependent root verdict
incidents.rule: Only an oracle-valued deadline is exempt from the override rule; include shared helpers in each dependent verdict.
incidents.signature: A timeout override hides in assertion options or a shared helper that a root depends on.

incidents.title: A marker generator listing every earlier unmarked root made a root approved later repeat an old path that a later marker already held
incidents.rule: Check uniqueness across all markers, and re-read inputs immediately before reporting.
incidents.signature: Two markers name the same old path because a generator listed all earlier unmarked roots.

incidents.title: Test discovery was compared with an absolute scratch prefix that matched by accident, and guard omission mutants were not each killed
incidents.rule: Compare relative names and kill every mutant on its own.
incidents.signature: A discovery comparison passes because an absolute prefix coincidentally lines up.

incidents.title: A document already at its hard size cap had no room for the next transcription, so the cap was met only after editing
incidents.rule: Plan against a hard cap before the edit, not after.
incidents.signature: An edit is made first and the size cap is discovered afterward.

incidents.title: Finished work sat for hours because replies never arrived, the clock was misread and worktrees were not swept
incidents.rule: Sweep the disk and read a real clock before trusting replies.
incidents.signature: Several teammates finish, no reply arrives, and the lead waits.

incidents.title: A syntax hygiene rule flagging every literal timer over one second also flagged a cancellation watchdog
incidents.rule: A hygiene rule should test intent, not only syntax.
incidents.signature: A rule against long timers rejects a bound that fails and is cleared.

incidents.title: An identity checker rejecting every shared destination across pending roots flagged inert drafts
incidents.rule: Enforce destination uniqueness where files become active.
incidents.signature: Two pending drafts name one destination and the checker fails.

incidents.title: A stage hang deadline copied from a planning estimate killed a correct run once heavier tests joined
incidents.rule: Measure, then set deadlines.
incidents.signature: A stage that passed earlier is killed after more tests are added.

incidents.title: Vitest 4 ran projects in parallel and file serialization inside a project did not order whole-cluster checks
incidents.rule: Serialize across projects explicitly when they share state.
incidents.signature: Inventory checks across a shared cluster race between projects.

incidents.title: A local guard behind a shared environment pin was masked, and a mutation claim was reasoned instead of measured
incidents.rule: Measure mutations and protect files first.
incidents.signature: Removing a guard changes nothing because an outer pin already covers it.

incidents.title: A QA case followed only 3xx redirects while Payload 3 admin redirects under Next 16 are soft redirects with HTTP 200
incidents.rule: Assert what the user sees, not the transport mechanism.
incidents.signature: A test expecting a 3xx fails on a correct redirect.

incidents.title: A QA-template line pasted into an engineer task contradicted the engineer commit duty
incidents.rule: One template per role.
incidents.signature: A task carries an instruction from another role template.

incidents.title: A cross-agent inventory flake came from sharing one harness cluster between runtime agents
incidents.rule: Give each agent its own cluster.
incidents.signature: Inventory checks fail when two agents use one cluster.

incidents.title: A database adapter created an absent database even with schema push disabled
incidents.rule: Make a missing database fail by name instead of creating it.
incidents.signature: A misspelled or missing database name silently becomes a new empty database.

incidents.title: A stage that kept a database alive collided with later inventory and frozen-clock gc cases
incidents.rule: Tie resource lifetime to its creating stage.
incidents.signature: A leftover database from one stage changes the result of a later stage.

incidents.title: A readiness deadline tested only inside a step was untested outside it
incidents.rule: Test the deadline on every path that can reach it.
incidents.signature: A deadline is proven on one code path and ships on another.

incidents.title: A known red was listed before checking the scan roots of the hygiene rule that raised it
incidents.rule: Confirm a rule scope before reporting its finding.
incidents.signature: A finding is recorded as a known failure without confirming the rule scans that file.

incidents.title: A static watchdog rule accepting only an inline await of a new promise flagged stored promises and other valid shapes
incidents.rule: Widen a rule by shape and prove it with near-miss negatives.
incidents.signature: A rule written against one syntax shape rejects equivalent valid code.

incidents.title: A redirect test searching for one allowed substring accepted a bad target beside a benign decoy
incidents.rule: Validate all candidates, not the first acceptable one.
incidents.signature: A redirect check passes because one acceptable string appears among several candidates.

incidents.title: Two branches implementing the same stage split were merged without re-measuring, although merged tests can change a project time several times over
incidents.rule: Re-measure after a merge that changes the tests in a stage.
incidents.signature: A merged stage split keeps timings measured before the merge.

incidents.title: Expected lifecycle refusals were mixed with static findings in a sweep
incidents.rule: Report expected refusals apart from real findings.
incidents.signature: A sweep report cannot tell an intended refusal from a real finding.

incidents.title: A readiness check measured the lead checkout while preship measures the Foundry clone
incidents.rule: Check the tree the gate actually reads.
incidents.signature: A readiness verdict is taken from one checkout and the gate reads another.

incidents.title: A truncated FAST run stopped at the first red stage and understated the stage sum by about half
incidents.rule: Measure the complete run before claiming a budget.
incidents.signature: A timing taken from a run that stopped early is used as a full measurement.

incidents.title: A moved history row was silently modernized instead of staying byte identical
incidents.rule: Separate source-preserving relocation from attributed status changes.
incidents.signature: A move that is described as byte identical changes a this version label.

incidents.title: ASCII-only fixtures could not tell UTF-16 code unit order from UTF-8 byte order
incidents.rule: Choose data that separates the alternatives under test.
incidents.signature: A sort or compare test passes under either ordering because all data is ASCII.

incidents.title: Marker SHA, reviewer approval scope, successor closure and activation ownership were treated as one fact
incidents.rule: One fact per field.
incidents.signature: A marker is read as proof of approval, closure and ownership at once.

incidents.title: A missing independently callable guard lacked protocol cases, and macOS path aliases looked like regressions
incidents.rule: Resolve paths before comparing, and compare to the active bytes first.
incidents.signature: A guard without its own tests and cwd assertions failing on path aliases.

incidents.title: A hygiene rule against conditional test omission needed a precise flagged and allowed set
incidents.rule: State both the flagged and the allowed set of a hygiene rule.
incidents.signature: A conditional skip or registration hides a test from the suite.

incidents.title: An exit code 2 advisory wording in the gate runner defaulted to proceed
incidents.rule: Override permissive defaults on the release path.
incidents.signature: A gate returns an advisory status that a caller treats as pass.

incidents.title: A test checked only the dispatch argv of a child stage, not its semantics
incidents.rule: Test what a stage does, not how it was started.
incidents.signature: A stage is proven by what it was called with, not by what it did.

incidents.title: A marker for an already activated revision used the pending path form
incidents.rule: Run the identity checker on the exact tree before committing any marker.
